skill.name: pubchem-database
skill.description: Query PubChem compounds, properties, structures, similarity searches, and bioactivity data through PubChemPy and PUG-REST.
skill.summary: Use PubChemPy and PUG-REST examples to retrieve chemical identifiers, properties, structures, annotations, and assay bioactivity.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 126 static findings were adjudicated as false positives based on file context. Network activity is expected PubChem access, and external-command findings are markdown backticks in documentation. The filesystem finding is a fixed-name example download, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Public network requests are central to the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Document that compound names, SMILES strings, CIDs, and assay queries are sent to PubChem services.

remediation.issue: The structure image example writes to a fixed local filename.
remediation.suggestion: Use a configurable output path, check before overwriting, and describe the file side effect near the example.

remediation.issue: Broad PubChem searches can create high request volume.
remediation.suggestion: Keep MaxRecords limits, rate limiting, and caching guidance visible in examples that query many compounds.

content.value_statement: Chemical research often needs reliable compound identifiers, properties, structures, and assay links. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical PubChem workflows using PubChemPy and PUG-REST.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to search PubChem by name, CID, SMILES, InChI, and formula.
Retrieves molecular properties such as weight, formula, XLogP, TPSA, and hydrogen bond counts.
Documents similarity and substructure search workflows with MaxRecords limits.
Provides helper functions for bioassay summaries, targets, active compounds, and annotations.
Includes rate-limit guidance for PubChem PUG-REST requests.
Shows how to download SDF, JSON, and PNG structures through PubChemPy or PUG-REST.
limitations: Requires internet access to PubChem or installed PubChemPy for most workflows.
Public PubChem data may be incomplete or unavailable for some compounds.
Large similarity and substructure searches can time out or take many seconds.
The skill provides research support, not medical, regulatory, or safety advice.

use_cases.title: Look Up Compound Properties
use_cases.description: Retrieve identifiers, formulas, molecular weights, SMILES strings, and selected descriptors for known compounds.

use_cases.title: Compare Candidate Molecules
use_cases.description: Build repeatable workflows for property comparison, drug-likeness checks, and batch compound screening.

use_cases.title: Explore Bioactivity Evidence
use_cases.description: Find PubChem assay summaries, target names, active compounds, and annotation sections for early discovery research.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Compound
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PubChem skill to find aspirin. Return its CID, formula, molecular weight, canonical SMILES, and common synonyms.

prompt_templates.title: Compare A Small Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare aspirin, ibuprofen, and naproxen with PubChemPy. Include CID, formula, molecular weight, XLogP, TPSA, HBD, and HBA.

prompt_templates.title: Search Similar Structures
prompt_templates.prompt: Find compounds similar to imatinib using PubChem similarity search. Use Threshold 85 and MaxRecords 20. Summarize useful candidate properties.

prompt_templates.title: Review Bioactivity Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bioactivity helper to summarize PubChem assay activity for CID 2244. Include active, inactive, inconclusive, and target details when available.

output_examples.input: Find identifiers and basic properties for aspirin.
output_examples.output: Returns PubChem CID 2244, formula C9H8O4, molecular weight 180.16, canonical SMILES, InChIKey, and selected synonyms.

output_examples.input: Compare drug-like properties for aspirin, ibuprofen, and naproxen.
output: Provides a table-style comparison of CID, formula, molecular weight, XLogP, TPSA, donor count, and acceptor count.
Notes missing PubChem values when a descriptor is unavailable.

output_examples.input: Summarize bioactivity for a PubChem compound ID.
output_examples.output: Reports total assays, activity outcome counts, representative assay names, and target information when PubChem provides it.

best_practices: Use PubChem CIDs when possible for repeatable lookups.
Set MaxRecords and add delays for broad searches.
Check missing fields before comparing properties.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad searches without result limits.
Do not treat PubChem assay activity as clinical evidence.
Do not send confidential compound structures to public services without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows query PubChem or use PubChemPy, which needs access to PubChem services.

faq.question: Can it search by SMILES?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for exact SMILES lookup, similarity search, and substructure search.

faq.question: Can it retrieve assay data?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script retrieves PubChem assay summaries, activity outcomes, target names, and active compound lists.

faq.question: Does it provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports chemical and bioactivity research workflows, but it does not validate medical, regulatory, or safety decisions.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it download structure files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show SDF, JSON, and PNG downloads using PubChemPy or direct PUG-REST requests.
